messages:
Maria L: Heads-up — after landing the int8 PTQ reranker build I'm seeing NDCG jitter between runs. baseline float ndcg@10 0.412, int8 runs vary 0.392 -> 0.403 -> 0.387. unclear if this is noise or a systemic tie-breaking issue.
Samir: ugh. did you run with the same seed and candidate ordering each time?
Maria L: same random seed for model init/eval harness, yes. but the candidate list order comes from upstream retrieval and can vary per job.
Ryan: could be nondet in tokenizer or batching too. I had a case where different batching changed KV-cache flush timing and slightly changed scores.
Helena: also check stable sort on embedding ties. our reranker uses a stable sort but downstream dedupe sometimes shuffles.
Maria L: good point. hypothesis: small score deltas around tie region get amplified by sorting/deterministic/non-deterministic ordering which changes NDCG. proposed steps: (1) force deterministic candidate ordering, (2) run float vs int8 with identical batching + tokenizer seeds, (3) compute per-query delta histogram and tie density.
Jon P: +1. for (1) we can sort candidates by doc_id before rerank to remove upstream variance.
Samir: I'll add a quick flag in eval harness: `--force-candidate-sort doc_id` and re-run 5 seeds.
EvalBot: CI job 4823 for branch rerank/ndcg-jitter started.
Maria L: sample command I'm running:
```
python -m eval.run 
  --model path/to/int8/checkpoint 
  --queries queries/holdout.jsonl 
  --candidates candidates/holdout.jsonl 
  --force-candidate-sort doc_id 
  --seed 42 
  --batch-size 64
```
Samir: when you post the run output, include `per_query_ndcg_delta.json` so we can see concentration near zero and tails.
Ryan: also add `--tokenizer-version v2` and `--disable-metadata-shuffle` flags. I saw tokenizer v1 vs v2 give tiny tokenization shifts for short queries.
Helena: if we still see jumps after determinism, next suspect is quantization nonlinearity by query length. split the holdout into short/medium/long and compare ndcg per slice.
Maria L: ran one quick split: short (<10 tokens) ndcg drop ~0.003, medium ~0.018, long ~0.025. means long queries are more sensitive.
Jon P: that pattern points at context truncation differences or attention kernel numeric instability when quantized. maybe try asymmetric quantization config or per-channel scale.
Samir: I'll run PTQ with per-channel scales and report back. can we also pin sequence length to 512 for both float/int runs?
Maria L: yes pinned seq_len=512. also logged raw logits to look for value clipping.
EvalBot: CI job 4823 passed tests. artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-evals/4823/
Ryan: nice. once we have the per-query deltas, let's compute how many queries cross rank thresholds (e.g., top1 changes) vs small score drift that doesn't affect ranking. that tells us if NDCG changes are ranking-impactful.
Helena: FYI, I pushed a tiny eval visualization to `gs://redwood-visuals/rdw-ndcg-jitter/` with waterfall plots to inspect tails.
Maria L: thanks all — I'll collect the runs and share a summary. next actions: Samir runs per-channel PTQ, Ryan does tokenizer-batch determinism check, Jon investigates attention kernel numeric tweaks. i'll compile per-query delta CSV and a short note for the oncall if we need to roll back the quantized model. :thumbsup:
Samir: on it.
Jon P: ping me the artifacts when ready, I'll look into kernel params.
Maria L: will do.
